political_impact.text: Three Arch Rocks, off Oceanside, Oregon, was reserved for the Department of Agriculture as a preserve for native birds and animals, the first federal bird reservation on the Pacific Coast.

legacy.text: The refuge sustains what the Fish and Wildlife Service calls the largest and most diverse seabird colony in Oregon, and the only Steller sea lion pupping site on the north Oregon coast.

today.name: Three Arch Rocks National Wildlife Refuge
today.note: Fifteen acres across nine rocks; also a designated wilderness since 1970.
today.source: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Public Law 91-504

legacy.text: Oil infrastructure overran East Timbalier Island, and by early summer 2021 it had "finally erod[ed] away," though Louisiana now lists its restoration among active projects.
legacy.source: USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2022–5107; CPRA Fiscal Year 2027 Annual Plan (March 2026)

today.name: East Timbalier Island Reservation
today.note: Never renamed a National Wildlife Refuge; revoked in 1969.

later_actions.text: Assistant Secretary of the Interior Harrison Loesch revoked the reservation by Public Land Order 4597, under delegated authority.
Louisiana's Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority closed a restoration project at the design stage after a breach and rising costs, moving the money to other barrier-island work.
The authority's Fiscal Year 2027 Annual Plan lists East Timbalier Island Restoration among active projects, in engineering and design.

related.note: Amended by the order of January 28, 1908.

uncertain: No text of the order is available online; only its date and subject are known.

political_impact.text: The orders drew little notice, but they belonged to the larger quarrel over executive reservations that critics called the President "locking up" the public domain by fiat.

legacy.text: The five orders are among the fifty-one bird reservations Roosevelt created by executive order, the practical foundation of the National Wildlife Refuge System.
legacy.source: National Park Service; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
